result.summary:
Scope test: still a tenant-data path (partition DDL/DML against tenant schemas) -- re-run, not skipped. This is a re-gate: read `git diff HEAD~2..HEAD -- lib/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance.ex` in full plus the diffs to docs/migration/decisions/0037-...md and lib/letflow/design/req376-partition-event-retirement.md. The change is a strict simplification: relocate_protected_rows/2 (INSERT into events_archive + DELETE from the retiring partition, wrapped in Repo.transaction/1) is replaced by count_protected_rows/2 (a single read-only `SELECT count(*)`), called after attach_partition!/4 completes instead of before detach_partition!/2. No new call sites, no new identifiers, no new data-access path -- code surface area shrank.

INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES, freshly re-verified against count_protected_rows/2. The function's only query is `SELECT count(*) FROM "#{schema_name}"."#{partition}" WHERE event_type = ANY($1)`. `schema_name` and `partition` are the exact same two arguments already threaded through every other function in this module (do_detached_standalone/6 and do_already_retired/4 both call it with the `schema_name` passed into retire_month/3 and the `partition` computed by partition_name/3 from typed year/month integers -- confirmed by reading both call sites in the diff) -- no new provenance to check, and provenance was already confirmed in the first-pass PASS (schema_name validated via TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1's `tenant_ + 32-hex` shape check before any query fires; partition is never caller-supplied free text). Each call is scoped to exactly one schema_name, exactly one partition table, identical to the module's existing pattern -- no cross-schema statement introduced. PASS.

INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation of tenant/user-controlled data) -- APPLIES, freshly re-verified. count_protected_rows/2 interpolates two identifiers (schema_name, partition) -- both system-derived per INV-1's finding above, same discipline as every other identifier interpolation already reviewed in this module (SQL has no bind-parameter syntax for identifiers, so interpolation is the only mechanism; the risk this invariant actually guards against -- caller-controlled data reaching an interpolated position -- doesn't apply since neither value is caller-controlled). The one genuine value in the query, `keep_forever_types` (the WHERE clause's event_type list), is passed as a real Postgrex bind parameter ($1), not interpolated -- same as the old relocate_protected_rows/2's equivalent SELECT. The removed code (INSERT into events_archive + DELETE from the partition, event_id/created_at lists as $1/$2 bind params) is gone entirely, not replaced with a new interpolation risk -- net reduction in raw-SQL surface, from 3 statements (SELECT, INSERT, DELETE) to 1 (SELECT). No new hit against `grep -rn "Repo.query" lib/letflow/event_store/partition_maintenance.ex`. PASS.

INV-2, INV-3, INV-5 -- NOT-APPLICABLE, unchanged from the first pass (no client-facing API response type, no scripting/plugin sandbox, no lookup-by-ID endpoint touched by this diff or the rework).

INV-4 (secrets by reference only) -- APPLIES (live), carried forward: this rework touches no config/env/secret-adjacent code at all -- confirmed by re-reading the diff, which is confined to partition_maintenance.ex's DML mechanism and two documentation files. No new grep needed; nothing in the changed surface could regress this. PASS.

INV-6 (new data-access paths prove their scoping) -- APPLIES, satisfied by this handoff (the meta-invariant) exactly as the first pass's handoff satisfied it for the original implementation.

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) -- APPLIES (live) for the same reachability boundary as the first pass: retire_month/3 (and everything it calls, including count_protected_rows/2) still has no live caller anywhere in this diff or the rework (confirmed by grep -rn 'retire_month' lib/ -- only the function definition and test/design-doc references, no Scheduler/Poller wiring) -- INV-8 has nothing new to apply to on the reachable path (ensure_future_partitions/2 via the Poller, unchanged by this rework). count_protected_rows/2 itself uses Repo.query!/2 (raising) consistent with the rest of this not-yet-wired module -- same MINOR note already carried to REVIEWER in the first pass, not a new BLOCKER; this rework does not change that call's reachability. PASS as applied.

INV-9 (tenant-controlled outbound URL validation) -- NOT-APPLICABLE, unchanged (no outbound HTTP touched).

Doc-diff security check (decision 0037's 'Implementation-discovered correction #2' section, design doc SS4.4/4.4a/4.5): read both diffs in full. Both are an honest, explicit scope-narrowing -- keep_forever rows are no longer physically relocated into events_archive_default (proven impossible in either DETACH-ordering by two independent real-Postgres 23514 check_violation reproductions, cited with evidence) and are instead carried across intact by the existing whole-partition DETACH+ATTACH, which decision 0037 already commits to never following with a DROP. This does not weaken any currently-live guarantee: EO-002's count-preserved invariant is explicitly re-verified against real Postgres in the same section (1 before, 1 after, across events UNION events_archive) and no DROP-capable purge tier exists yet for the abandoned relocation mechanism to have protected against. Both docs explicitly flag the deferred future-tier work rather than silently dropping it -- no misleading claim survives in either document (design doc's own table at the bottom, mapping EO-002 to SS4.4, is updated in the same diff to say 'read-only' rather than leaving stale 'relocation' language). No security-invariant consequence beyond INV-1/INV-7 already assessed above; this is REVIEWER's architecture-soundness call (already flagged in the docs as re-entering Step 2d), not a SECURITY-REVIEWER concern.

Overall: no applicable invariant failed. The rework is a net reduction in SQL-statement surface (1 SELECT instead of SELECT+INSERT+DELETE) using identical, already-verified identifier provenance -- nothing about this diff introduces new risk on any invariant.
